overview.description: Four Card Brag is the four-card variation of Three Card Brag: each player is dealt four cards, discards one face down, and plays the best three-card Brag hand, with the discard used only to break exact ties.

history.origins: 4-Card Brag developed as a popular regional variant in the UK, designed to provide more player agency than the strictly deterministic deal of 3-Card Brag. It is particularly common in casual pub games where players want slightly 'bigger' hands to play with.
timeline: Mid-20th Century: Multi-card Brag variants gain popularity in British card clubs.
1980s: Standardized as a common Dealer's Choice option.
Present: A frequent favorite in online Brag communities.
history.evolution: The game retains all the core 'Blind' and 'See' rules of its parent but adds a 'Pre-Vying' phase where hands are optimized.
history.cultural: Reflects the British preference for card games that allow for skill-based selection and tactical 'mucking'.

setup.equipment: Standard pack, betting chips or currency.
setup.dealing: Deal four cards face-down to each player. Players choose three to keep and place the fourth face-down in a shared muck pile.

rules.objective: Win the pot by forming the best three-card hand from the four dealt, or by forcing others to fold.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Selection**: Players receive 4 cards and discard 1. 2. **Vying**: Standard Brag betting follows. Players choose to play 'Blind' (without looking at their chosen 3) or 'See'. 3. **Ranks**: Prial > Running Flush > Run > Flush > Pair > High Card.
keyRules: The choice of which three cards to keep is the only skill difference from 3-Card Brag.
Equal hands favor the player who remained Blind longer.

strategy.basic: Prioritize pairs and consecutive suits when choosing your three cards. A low pair is often better than three high unconnected cards.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Hidden' Kicker: If you have a choice of two identical pairs (e.g., two 8s and a 10 vs two 8s and a 4), always keep the highest kicker to win tie-breaking showdowns.
strategy.advanced: Discard Influence: Track which ranks are being mucked. If you see several players mucking 3s, the probability of someone holding a Prial of 3s (the top hand) drops significantly.
tips: Don't spend too long choosing; the core of the game is still the betting phase.
If you are dealt three of a kind in your four cards, keep them! It's an automatic Prial.

list.name: 5-Card Brag
list.description: Players receive five cards and choose three, leading to even stronger average hands.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Engine differences for 5-Card Brag are not yet modeled as overrides in this file.

difficulty.easy: Chooses the three highest cards regardless of combinations. Always sees cards immediately.
difficulty.medium: Identifies pairs and runs in the initial 4 cards. Stays blind for 1 round.
difficulty.hard: Optimizes the 3-card hand for long-term equity. Tracks mucked cards. Expert at blind bluffing.

considerations: Betting logic must account for the higher average hand strength compared to 3-Card Brag.

additional: Official Rules of Card Games (Bicycle Edition)

ante.description: Contribute a fixed amount to the pot before the deal.
ante.constraints: Allowed only during the ante phase.

deal.reason: The initial distribution of four cards to each player is performed automatically by the system dealer.

reveal_market.reason: 4-Card Brag is a hole-card game where all cards are held privately; no shared market exists.

buy_market.reason: Players cannot purchase cards from a market; hand optimization is restricted to the selection phase.

buy_stock.reason: There is no drawing or buying from the stock during play; the round uses the four cards dealt at the start.

fold.description: Abandon the hand and forfeit all chips in the pot.
fold.constraints: Allowed during the vying phase when facing a bet.

check.reason: Standard Brag requires an active bet to remain in the hand; checking is generally not supported.

call.description: Match the current bet level (price depends on whether player is Blind or Seeing).
call.constraints: Allowed only during the vying phase.

bet.description: Place or increase a wager into the pot.
bet.constraints: Seeing players must bet at least double the Blind bet amount.

raise.description: Increase the size of the current bet.

declare.reason: Hand results are established during the showdown comparison rather than through a formal declaration.

reveal_hand.reason: The system automatically reveals hands at the request of a player who pays the 'See' double-cost.

award_pot.description: Distribute the pot to the winner at showdown or the last player standing.

play_card.reason: 4-Card Brag is a vying/poker game where cards are held rather than played to tricks.

draw.reason: All four cards are received at the start; no drawing phase exists during the play of the hand.

discard.description: Place one card from the hand face-down into the muck during the selection phase.
discard.constraints: Mandatory to reach the three-card hand size.

pass.reason: Players must either bet, see, or fold during their turn; a simple pass is not supported.

bid.reason: Brag uses a wagering system rather than an auction-style bidding system for contracts.

meld.reason: Hand resolution is based strictly on three-card poker hierarchies rather than forming melds.

go_out.reason: The hand terminates only after a showdown occurs or all but one player have folded.

notApplicableReasons.drawConfig: Standard 4-card Brag does not include a draw pile or exchange mechanic after the initial selection.
notApplicableReasons.specialCards: Cards contribute only their rank and suit values to hand combinations; no individual card has a secondary effect.
notApplicableReasons.declarationMechanism: Wagering results are immediate and public; no hidden tokens are required.
notApplicableReasons.fishingConfig: 4-Card Brag is a vying/poker game and does not use a capture-from-tableau fishing mechanic.
notApplicableReasons.meldConfig: Points are earned only through hand ranking comparison; no melding occurs in the game.
notApplicableReasons.shedding: This game is not a shedding game; players maintain their hands throughout the deal.

customActions.description: Distribute four cards to each player at the start of the round.
Select the optimal three cards to form the Brag hand.
Bet on the hand without looking at the chosen three cards.
Pay double price to see the cards before betting.
Bet on the hand after paying to see the cards.
Request a showdown to determine the winner between remaining players.
Compare the three-card hands according to Brag hierarchy rules.

engine.handRankingSystem: None; specialized Brag hierarchy determines the winning hand at showdown.
engine.deckDescription: One standard 52-card deck consisting of four suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs), each with thirteen ranks from ace down to two. No jokers; used for four-card Brag where prials (three of a kind), runs, and flushes are ranked and ace may be high or low in runs.
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs). Flushes (four of the same suit) and running flushes (four consecutive ranks in the same suit) are ranked hands. Suits do not break ties between equal hand types in Brag.
engine.rankDescription: Thirteen ranks per suit; for prials the three is the highest rank, then two, ace, king down to four. For runs, ace may be high or low. Standard Brag order: prial of threes best, then runs, then flushes, then pairs, then high card.

hero.title: 4-CARD BRAG
hero.subtitle: The Strategic Vyer
hero.tagline: Four cards dealt. Three kept. One choice to rule them all.

synthesis.shortDescription: A tactical variation of standard Brag that grants players more agency. Every player receives four cards and must choose the best three to take into battle. This selection phase deepens the strategy, leading to higher-ranked showdowns and more intense bluffing rounds.

prompts.human: You were dealt the 3♠, 3♣, King of Hearts, and 3♦. You have a Prial of 3s—the highest hand in the game! Discard the King and prepare to build a massive pot.
prompts.ai: Game: 4-Card Brag. Type: Vying. Rules: 4 dealt, 3 kept. Hierarchy: Prial > Running Flush > Run. Half-price blind betting. Choice phase added to parent 3-card game.

scoring.winCondition: Last player standing or best three-card hand at showdown.

penalties.Forced Fold: A player who is 'Seen' and holds the weaker hand is forced to fold immediately.

scoring.splitRules: Tied hands split the pot equally.

nullReasons.targetScore: No fixed target score; play until the session concludes.
nullReasons.cardValues: Individual cards determine hand rankings rather than having point values.
